info.title: Orvano
info.description: The Orvano API. Every path lives under /v1.

post.description: Signs a new user up with an email and password, and signs them in.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Gets the signed in user. A server can call it with a user's access token to check that the session is still active.

patch.description: Changes the signed in user's name or metadata.

post.description: Deletes the signed in user with all their sessions. It can't be undone.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

put.description:
Starts changing the signed in user's email: emails a confirmation link to the new address. The email changes
when that link is opened.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Emails a 6 digit sign in code that works for 10 minutes. An email without a user gets one that creates the user,
unless `createUser` is false. The answer is the same 202 either way.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Changes a user's email to the new address with the token from the confirmation link, and marks it verified. It
needs no session and keeps every session. The token works once.

Emails a sign in link. An email without a user gets one that creates the user, unless `createUser` is false. The
answer is the same 202 either way, so it never tells anyone which emails have accounts.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

put.description: Changes the signed in user's password and ends every other session of theirs.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
Emails a password reset link, if the email belongs to an active user. The answer is the same 202 whether or not
it does, so it never tells anyone which emails have accounts.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Sets a new password with the token from a reset link, and signs the user in. Every other session of the user
ends, and the email counts as verified. The token works once.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Lists the signed in user's active sessions, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Sessions per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

delete.description: Ends every session of the signed in user except the current one.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

delete.description: Signs out: ends the current session.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Signs a user in with an emailed code. After 5 wrong tries the code stops working; ask for a new one.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description: Signs a user in with the token from a magic link, creating them when the link was for a new email. The token works once.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description: Signs a user in with their email and password.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description: Trades the current refresh token for a new pair. The old token keeps answering with the same pair for 10 seconds, so a retry is safe.

delete.description: Ends one of the signed in user's sessions.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Emails the signed in user a link that verifies their email.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.description:
Verifies a user's email with the token from a verification link. It needs no session and creates none; a client
signed in as that user refreshes its session, so the access token's claim changes at once. The token works once.

Creates a console account and signs it in, setting the session cookies. The install's sign up policy decides
who may: the first account (with the setup token when the install has one), anyone while sign up is open, or
an invitation.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Gets the signed in console account.

post.description: Signs a console account in with its email and password, setting the session cookies.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

delete.description: Signs out: ends the console session and clears both cookies.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Trades the refresh cookie for a new pair of session cookies. The console client calls it after `token_expired`.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: Lists the console's own emails (invites) from the last 30 days, newest first. Install admins only.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the page before; omit for the first page.

get.description: Gets the install settings. Install admins only.

patch.description: Changes the install settings. Install admins only.

get.description:
Tells whether the install still waits for its first admin. Needs no console session, so the console can
send you to the setup screen before anyone can sign in.
Gets the install's SMTP settings. Install admins only.

put.description:
Saves the install's SMTP settings, replacing any stored ones. Install admins only. A private network address
is allowed here, since the install admin already controls the server.

delete.description:
Deletes the install's SMTP settings, so projects without their own can't send email. Install admins only.
Answers 204 also when nothing is stored.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
Sends a test email to your own console email through the given settings, saved or not, and stores nothing.
Install admins only. Waits at most 20 seconds and never retries.

Joins the org with the signed in console account, whose email must be the invitation's (ignoring case), and
uses the invitation up. A member already in the org keeps their role.

Shows what an invite link is for. Needs no console session, only the token. Fails with
`invitation_not_found` for a used, replaced, or revoked link, and `invitation_expired` after it expired.

get.description: Lists the orgs the caller is a member of, deleting ones included.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Orgs per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

post.description: Creates an org with the caller as its owner.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Gets one org the caller is a member of.

patch.description: Renames an org. Owners only; fails with `org_not_active` while the org is deleting.

delete.description:
Deletes an org: it moves to `deleting` and is purged after the grace period. Owners only. Fails with
`org_not_empty` while any of its projects is not deleting.

get.description: Lists the org's invitations, pending and expired, oldest first. Owners only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Invitations per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

post.description:
Invites an email to the org with a role and returns the link to share, once. Owners only. Inviting an email
again replaces its old invitation, whose link stops working. Fails with `already_member` when that email's
console account is already a member, and `invitation_limit` past 100 invitations.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

delete.description: Revokes an invitation, so its link stops working at once. Owners only.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: Lists the org's members, oldest first. Any member.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Members per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

patch.description:
Changes a member's role. Owners only. Fails with `last_owner` when it would demote the org's last owner.
Takes effect on the member's next request.

delete.description:
Removes a member from the org, or lets a member leave when `userId` is their own. Owners remove anyone; every
member may leave. Fails with `last_owner` when it would leave the org without an owner. The member's access
ends on their next request; API keys they created keep working.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: Lists an org's projects, deleting ones included.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Projects per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

post.description:
Creates a project in `provisioning`; it turns `active` once its database schema exists. Owners and
developers; fails with `org_not_active` while the org is deleting.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.description: Restores a deleting org before its purge. Owners only. Its projects are restored one by one.

get.description: Gets the project named by `X-Orvano-Project`, in any state.

patch.description: Renames the project. Owners and developers.

delete.description:
Deletes the project: it stops being served at once and is purged after the grace period, with its
data, keys, platforms, and users. Owners only.

get.description: Lists the token signing keys of the project named by `X-Orvano-Project`. Every role.

post.description:
Rotates the project's signing key: a new key signs from now on, and the old one keeps verifying the tokens it
signed for 24 hours, then leaves. Owners only.

get.description: Gets the SMTP settings of the project named by `X-Orvano-Project`, and whose settings it sends through.

put.description:
Saves the project's own SMTP settings, replacing any stored ones. Owners and developers. Fails with
`smtp_host_not_allowed` when the host is, or resolves to, a private network address.

delete.description:
Deletes the project's own SMTP settings, so it sends through the install's, if any. Owners and developers.
Answers 204 also when nothing is stored.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
Sends a test email to your own console email through the given settings, saved or not, and stores nothing.
Owners and developers. Waits at most 20 seconds and never retries; a failure answers `smtp_unreachable`,
`smtp_tls_failed`, `smtp_auth_failed`, `smtp_rejected`, or `smtp_timeout`.

get.description: Lists the four auth email templates of the project named by `X-Orvano-Project`. Any member.
Gets one template: the project's own version, or the default. Any member. An unknown `kind` answers `not_found`.

put.description:
Saves the project's own version of a template, replacing any stored one (the last save wins). Owners and
developers. Fails with `template_invalid` when a part does not parse, names an unknown variable or filter, or
is too costly to render.

delete.description: Deletes the project's own version, so the default is used again. Owners and developers. Answers 204 also when it is already the default.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Renders the given content, saved or not, with the sample values, and stores nothing. Owners and developers.

get.description: Lists the emails of the project named by `X-Orvano-Project` from the last 30 days, newest first. Any member.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the page before; omit for the first page.

get.description: Lists the API keys of the project named by `X-Orvano-Project`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Keys per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

post.description:
Creates an API key and returns its secret, once. Owners and developers; fails with `project_not_ready` while
the project is being deleted, and `org_not_active` while the org is.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

delete.description:
Deletes an API key, which stops it working at once. Owners delete any key, developers their own; still allowed
while the project is being deleted, but fails with `org_not_active` while the org is.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: Lists the platforms of the project named by `X-Orvano-Project`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Platforms per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

post.description:
Adds a platform. Owners and developers; fails with `project_not_ready` while the project is being deleted, and
`org_not_active` while the org is.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

patch.description:
Renames a platform or changes its identifier. Owners and developers; fails with `project_not_ready` while the
project is being deleted, and `org_not_active` while the org is.

delete.description:
Removes a platform. Owners and developers; still allowed while the project is being deleted, but fails with
`org_not_active` while the org is.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Restores a deleting project before its purge; it passes through `provisioning`. Owners only.
Retries provisioning a `failed` project. Owners and developers.
Retries the purge of a deleting project whose purge ran out of attempts. Owners and install admins.

get.description: Lists the users of the project named by `X-Orvano-Project`, newest first. Every role.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Only users whose email starts with this, ignoring case.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only users with this status: `active` or `blocked`.

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description: Only users created after this time.

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description: Only users created before this time.

parameters.name: emailVerified
parameters.description: Only verified users (true) or unverified users (false).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Users per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

post.description: Creates a user with an email and password. It does not sign them in.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Gets a user.

delete.description: Deletes a user with their password and sessions. It can't be undone.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Blocks a user: ends every session and refuses sign in. Blocking a blocked user changes nothing.

put.description: Changes a user's email at once, without a confirmation email. Owners and developers.
Marks a user's email verified or unverified. Owners and developers.

post.description: Emails a user a password reset link. Owners and developers.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

get.description: Lists a user's active sessions, newest first. `current` is always false.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Sessions per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

delete.description: Ends every session of a user.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

delete.description: Ends one session of a user.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Unblocks a user so they can sign in again. Their old sessions stay ended.
Emails a user a link that verifies their email. Owners and developers.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

get.description: Answers `{ status: ok }` to a valid console session.
Checks that the server is up and returns its version.
Gets a project's public signing keys, to check its access tokens.
Gets a project's discovery document, for JWT libraries that configure themselves from the issuer.

post.description: Always answers 409 with code `test_conflict`.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: Waits up to 15 seconds for the newest email to `to` that Mailpit caught after `after`, and reads it.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only an email received after this time.

get.description: Pages through five fixed items.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 2.

get.description: Lists the project's users, newest first.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Only users whose email starts with this, ignoring case.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only users with this status: `active` or `blocked`.

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description: Only users created after this time.

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description: Only users created before this time.

parameters.name: emailVerified
parameters.description: Only verified users (true) or unverified users (false).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Users per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.description: Gets a user.

delete.description: Deletes a user with their password and sessions. It can't be undone.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description: Blocks a user: ends every session and refuses sign in. Blocking a blocked user changes nothing.

put.description:
Changes a user's email at once, without a confirmation email. It deletes the user's live email links and codes,
and keeps their sessions.
Marks a user's email verified or unverified. Marking it verified deletes any live verification links.

post.description: Emails a user a password reset link.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

get.description: Lists a user's active sessions, newest first. `current` is always false.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Sessions per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

delete.description: Ends every session of a user.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

delete.description: Ends one session of a user.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

Emails a user a link that verifies their email.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

org.description: The org, with the caller's role in it.

alreadyMember.description: True when the caller was already a member; their role did not change.

AcceptedInvitation.description: The org an accepted invitation joined.

name.description: A name to recognize the key by, 1 to 100 characters.

prefix.description: The first 12 characters of the secret, to tell keys apart.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working; null for never.

lastUsedAt.description: When the key was last used, to the minute; null if never.

createdByUserId.description: The console user who created the key.

createdBy.description: The console user who created the key, with their name and email; null when that account no longer exists.

ApiKey.description: An API key for server code. Its secret is never shown again after creation.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

ApiKeyPage.description: One page of a project's API keys, oldest first.

ApiKeyScope.description:
What an API key may do: `<resource>.<read|write>`. A `write` scope does not imply `read`. Each product
adds its own scopes.

AuthEmailKind.description: One of the four auth email templates a project can edit.

isNewUser.description: Whether this call created the user: true from sign up, and from a magic link or email code for a new email.

verificationEmail.description: What happened to the verification email sign up was asked to send; null when none was asked for.

AuthResult.description: A signed in user and their new session.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

password.description: The new password: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

CompleteRecoveryRequest.description: A password reset, with the token from the emailed link.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

ConfirmEmailChangeRequest.description: An email change confirmation, with the token from the link sent to the new address.

email.description: The email, as typed at sign up; null for a user without one.

emailVerified.description: Whether the email has been verified. Also the access token's `email_verified` claim.

emailVerifiedAt.description: When the email was verified; null while it is not.

name.description: The display name; null when none was given.

status.description: Whether the user may sign in.

metadata.description: Your own data about the user: a JSON object of at most 16 KB.

lastSignInAt.description: When the user last signed in; null if never.

isInstallAdmin.description: True when the account is an install admin, who may change the install settings.

ConsoleAccount.description: A console account: a user of the console, and whether it is an install admin.

ConsoleSignupMode.description: Who may create a console account.

name.description: The display name; null when none was given.

ConsoleUserRef.description: A console account and the name and email it goes by, for showing who did something.

email.description: The email, trimmed, at most 320 characters. Unique in the project, ignoring case.

password.description: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

name.description: A display name, at most 256 characters.

verificationRedirectUrl.description:
When set, also emails a verification link that opens here: a host that is one of the project's web platforms, or
your app's own scheme. `AuthResult.verificationEmail` says whether it was sent.

CreateAccountRequest.description: A new user with an email and password.

name.description: A name to recognize the key by; trimmed, 1 to 100 characters.

scopes.description: What the key may do; at least one scope.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working, in the future; null or absent for never.

email.description: The email, trimmed, at most 320 characters. Unique among console accounts, ignoring case.

password.description: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

name.description: A display name, at most 256 characters.

inviteToken.description:
The token of the invitation this sign up came from, if any. The account then joins the invitation's org with
its role, whatever the sign up mode; the email must be the invitation's.

setupToken.description: The setup token from the installer's setup link; needed only for the install's first account.

email.description: The console account's email; case does not matter.

CreateConsoleSessionRequest.description: A console sign in with an email and password.

email.description: The email to sign in as; case does not matter.

createUser.description: Whether the code may create a user for an email that has none. Defaults to true.

CreateEmailCodeRequest.description: A request to email a 6 digit sign in code.

email.description: The email the code was sent to; case does not matter.

code.description: The 6 digit code from the email.

CreateEmailCodeSessionRequest.description: A sign in with an emailed code.

email.description: The email to invite; trimmed, at most 320 characters. Inviting an email again replaces its old invitation.
The email to sign in as; case does not matter.

redirectUrl.description:
Your page that receives the link, on a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on
`localhost` or `127.0.0.1`). The link adds `orvano_type=magic_link` and `orvano_token` to it.

createUser.description: Whether the link may create a user for an email that has none. Defaults to true.

CreateMagicLinkRequest.description: A request to email a sign in link.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

CreateMagicLinkSessionRequest.description: A sign in with the token from a magic link.

name.description: The org name; trimmed, 1 to 100 characters.

CreateOrgRequest.description: A new org. The caller becomes its owner.

email.description: The email the user signed up with; case does not matter.

CreatePasswordSessionRequest.description: A sign in with an email and password.

name.description: A name to recognize it by; trimmed, 1 to 100 characters.

identifier.description: The host pattern or app ID; see `Platform.identifier`.

CreatePlatformRequest.description: A new platform. Unique per project, type, and identifier, ignoring case.

name.description: The project name; trimmed, 1 to 100 characters.

email.description: The email of the account; case does not matter.

redirectUrl.description:
Your page that receives the link, on a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on
`localhost` or `127.0.0.1`). The link adds `orvano_type=recovery` and `orvano_token` to it.

CreateRecoveryRequest.description: A request to email a password reset link.

redirectUrl.description:
The page that receives the link, on a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on `localhost`
or `127.0.0.1`). The link adds `orvano_type=recovery` and `orvano_token` to it.

CreateUserRecoveryRequest.description: A request to email a user a password reset link.

email.description: The email, trimmed, at most 320 characters. Unique in the project, ignoring case.

password.description: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

name.description: A display name, at most 256 characters.

emailVerified.description: True to create the user with their email already verified, as when importing accounts. Defaults to false.

CreateUserRequest.description: A new user with an email and password, created by a server. No session is created.

redirectUrl.description:
The page that receives the link: a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on `localhost` or
`127.0.0.1`), or the app's own scheme. The link adds `orvano_type=verification` and `orvano_token` to it.

CreateUserVerificationRequest.description: A request to email a user a link that verifies their email.

redirectUrl.description:
Your page that receives the link: a host that is one of the project's web platforms (`http` only on `localhost`
or `127.0.0.1`), or your app's own scheme (its iOS, Android, or macOS identifier). The link adds
`orvano_type=verification` and `orvano_token` to it.

CreateVerificationRequest.description: A request to email a verification link to the signed in user.

secret.description: The secret to send as the API key: `orv_sk_` plus 43 characters. Store it now; it can't be shown again.

CreatedApiKey.description: A new API key with its secret. The secret is shown only here, once.

url.description: The link to share with the invited person. Anyone holding it can see the invitation until it is used or expires.

emailed.description: True when the server is also sending the link to the invited address by email (the install has an SMTP server).

CreatedInvitation.description: A new invitation and its link. The link is shown only here, once.

password.description: The user's current password. A user without one leaves it out, and must have signed in within 10 minutes.

DeleteAccountRequest.description: A request to delete the signed in user.

EmailFailureCode.description: Why an email was not sent.

EmailLinkType.description:
What an emailed link is for: the `orvano_type` parameter Orvano adds to every link it emails, beside
`orvano_token`. The SDKs' link helpers (`redeemLink`, `handleLink`) read it to call the right operation.

recipient.description: The recipient, masked: the first character, then `***`, then the domain.

status.description: Where it is in its delivery.

smtpSource.description: Whose SMTP settings sent it; null until it is sent.

attempts.description: How many times the server tried to send it.

errorCode.description: Why it was not sent; null unless `status` is `failed`.

completedAt.description: When it was sent or failed; null while it is queued.

EmailLogEntry.description: One email in the log. The recipient is masked, and the content is never kept.

nextCursor.description: The cursor of the next page; null on the last one.

EmailPage.description: One page of the email log, newest first.

name.description: The name shown beside it, if any.

EmailSender.description: Who an email is sent as.

EmailStatus.description: Where an email is in its delivery.

locale.description: The template's language. Always `en` for now.

subject.description: The subject line, a Liquid template.

html.description: The HTML part, a Liquid template.

text.description: The plain text part; null when it is generated from the HTML.

isCustom.description: True when the project edited it; false for the default.

updatedAt.description: When it was last edited; null for the default.

variables.description: The values this template can use.

EmailTemplate.description: One auth email template: the project's own version, or the default when it has none.

EmailTemplateCatalog.description: The auth email templates of a project. Always all four, so it is not paged.

subject.description: The subject line, 1 to 255 characters. It is not HTML encoded.

html.description: The HTML part, at most 100 KB. Every `{{ }}` output in it is HTML encoded.

text.description: The plain text part, at most 100 KB; null to generate it from the HTML.

EmailTemplateInput.description: A template's content to save, preview, or test. Each part is a Liquid template.

EmailTemplateName.description: Which email was sent: one of the four auth templates, or the console's own invite.

name.description: Its name.

examples: Sent when a user asks to reset their password.

isCustom.description: True when the project edited it; false for the default.

updatedAt.description: When it was last edited; null for the default.

sentTo.description: The address the test email went to: your own console email.

EmailTestResult.description: The result of a test email.

ErrorCode.description: Every stable error code the server sends in `Problem.code`.

Health.description: Whether the server is up, and which Orvano version it runs.

consoleSignup.description: Who may create a console account.

setupRequired.description: True while no install admin exists: the first console account must come from the installer's setup link.

signupOpen.description: True when anyone who can reach the console may create an account (`consoleSignup` is `open`).

InstallSetup.description: Whether the install still waits for its first admin.

settings.description: The install's settings; null when none are set.

InstallSmtp.description: The SMTP server of the whole install, which every project without its own sends through.

email.description: The email the invitation is for, as typed. Only a console account with this email, ignoring case, can use it.

invitedBy.description: The owner who created it; null when that console account no longer exists.

status.description: Whether it can still be accepted.

expiresAt.description: When the invitation stops working, 7 days after it was created.

Invitation.description: An invitation to join an org. Its link is shown only once, when it is created.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

InvitationPage.description: One page of an org's invitations, oldest first.

email.description: The email the invitation is for.

invitedByName.description: The inviter's name, else their email; null when that console account no longer exists.

InvitationPreview.description: What an invite link is for, shown before joining.

InvitationStatus.description: Whether an invitation can still be accepted.

InvitationTokenRequest.description: An invitation token, from the fragment of an invite link.

x.description: The public point's x coordinate, base64url.

y.description: The public point's y coordinate, base64url.

kid.description: The key ID, the `kid` in a token's header.

Jwk.description: One public signing key, as a JSON Web Key (RFC 7517).

Jwks.description: A project's public signing keys: the active key and any key retired within the last 24 hours.

name.description: The display name; null when none was given.

status.description: Whether the member's account may sign in.

role.description: The member's role in this org.

joinedAt.description: When the member joined the org.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

MemberPage.description:
One page of an org's members, oldest first. A member whose console account no longer exists is left out, so a
page can hold fewer items than the limit, even none, while `nextCursor` is still set.

MemberStatus.description: Whether a member's console account may sign in.

issuer.description: The issuer, the `iss` of every access token of the project.

OpenIdConfiguration.description:
The discovery document standard JWT libraries configure themselves from. Orvano is not an OpenID provider;
this exists so tools that take an issuer URL find the keys. Its names are the standard snake case ones.

name.description: The org name, 1 to 100 characters.

status.description: Whether the org is in use or being deleted.

role.description: The calling console user's role in this org.

deletedAt.description: When the org was deleted; null unless `deleting`.

purgeAfter.description: When a deleted org is purged for good; null unless `deleting`.

Org.description: An org: the owner of projects and the unit teammates join.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

OrgPage.description: One page of the caller's orgs, oldest first.

OrgRole.description: A console member's one role in an org.

name.description: A name to recognize it by, 1 to 100 characters.

identifier.description:
Web: a hostname (`app.example.com`), `*.` plus a hostname of at least two labels, `localhost`, or an IPv4
address, matched on any scheme and port. Android: the package name. iOS and macOS: the bundle ID.
Windows and Linux: a label.

Platform.description: An app allowed to use a project.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

PlatformPage.description: One page of a project's platforms, oldest first.

title.description: The standard HTTP reason phrase for the status.

detail.description: A short, safe sentence about this occurrence, when the server has one.

code.description: Orvano's stable error code, from the `ErrorCode` catalog. SDKs treat it as a plain string.

requestId.description: The request ID to quote when reporting a problem; also sent as `X-Request-Id`.

Problem.description:
An RFC 9457 problem details body. Every operation declares it as its `default` response, sent
as `application/problem+json`.

id.description: The project ID, 20 characters of `a` to `z` and `0` to `9`. Sent as `X-Orvano-Project`.

orgId.description: The org that owns the project.

name.description: The project name, 1 to 100 characters.

status.description: Where the project is in its lifecycle.

deletedAt.description: When the project was deleted; null unless `deleting`.

purgeAfter.description: When a deleted project is purged for good; null unless `deleting`.

purgeFailedAt.description: When the purge ran out of attempts; an owner can retry it. Null otherwise.

Project.description: A project: one app's isolated backend.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

ProjectPage.description: One page of an org's projects, oldest first.

source.description: Whose settings the project uses right now.

settings.description: The project's own settings; null unless `source` is `project`.

installSender.description: Who the install's own SMTP sends as, whenever the install has one; null when it has none.

ProjectSmtp.description: The SMTP settings a project sends email through.

RefreshSessionRequest.description: A trade of a refresh token for a new pair.

examples: Reset your password for Acme Shop

text.description: The rendered text part, generated from the HTML when the template has none.

RenderedEmail.description: A template rendered with the sample values.

lastRefreshedAt.description: When the session last traded its refresh token.

userAgent.description: The user agent that signed in, at most 512 characters; null when none was sent.

sdk.description: The SDK that signed in, from `X-Orvano-SDK`; null when none was sent.

ipAddress.description: The IP address last seen for the session; null when unknown.

current.description: Whether this is the session making the call.

Session.description: An active session of a user: one signed in device or browser.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

SessionPage.description: One page of a user's active sessions, newest first.

accessToken.description: An ES256 JWT, valid for 15 minutes.

refreshToken.description: Trades itself for a new pair once; keep it secret.

refreshTokenExpiresAt.description: When the session ends unless it refreshes first: 30 days idle, or 365 days after sign in.

sessionId.description: The session ID, also the `sid` claim of the access token.

SessionTokens.description:
A session's tokens. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer`; trade the refresh token for a new pair
before the access token expires. The SDKs do both for you.

id.description: The key ID, the `kid` of the tokens it signs.

status.description: `active` signs new tokens; `retiring` only verifies them until `retireAfter`.

retireAfter.description: When a retiring key leaves the JWKS; null for the active key.

SigningKey.description: A project's token signing key as the console shows it; never the key itself.

SigningKeys.description: A project's signing keys, the active one first.

SmtpSecurity.description: How the connection to the SMTP server is secured.

username.description: The username, if the server needs one.

hasPassword.description: True when a password is stored.

fromEmail.description: The address emails are sent from.

fromName.description: The name shown beside the From address.

replyTo.description: Where replies go; null means the From address.

SmtpSettings.description: Stored SMTP settings. The password is never returned.

host.description: The SMTP server: a host name, or an IPv4 or IPv6 address (no brackets). At most 253 characters.

username.description: The username to sign in with; null for a server that needs none. Needs `starttls` or `tls`.

password.description:
The password. Null keeps the stored one, which works only while the host, port, and username are the stored
ones; change any of them and you must send the password again.

fromEmail.description: The address emails are sent from.

fromName.description: The name shown beside the From address; null for none. At most 128 characters.

replyTo.description: Where replies go; null to use the From address.

SmtpSettingsInput.description: SMTP settings to save or to test.

SmtpSource.description: Whose SMTP settings a project sends through.

name.description: The name to write between `{{` and `}}`.

sample.description: The value previews and test emails use.

TemplateVariable.description: A value a template can use.

type.description: The `orvano_type` of the first link carrying `orvano_token`; null when there is none.

token.description: The `orvano_token` of that link; null when there is none.

code.description: The first run of exactly 6 digits, when the email has no such link; null otherwise.

url.description: That link in full; null when there is none.

TestEmail.description: The newest email Mailpit caught for an address, read from its text part.

TestErrorCode.description: Error codes only the test operations send. Generated only into the scenario runners.

TestItem.description: One fixed item in the `test.list` page.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

name.description: A new display name of at most 256 characters, or null to remove it.

metadata.description: New metadata, replacing the old: a JSON object of at most 16 KB.

UpdateAccountRequest.description: Changes to the signed in user. A field left out stays as it is.

email.description: The new email, trimmed, at most 320 characters.

redirectUrl.description:
Your page that receives the confirmation link: a host that is one of the project's web platforms, or your app's
own scheme. The link adds `orvano_type=email_change` and `orvano_token` to it.

password.description: The user's current password. A user without one leaves it out, and must have signed in within 10 minutes.

UpdateEmailRequest.description: A request to change the signed in user's email. It changes once the link sent to the new address is opened.

verified.description: True marks it verified (keeping an earlier date); false marks it unverified.

UpdateEmailVerificationRequest.description: Sets whether a user's email is verified.

consoleSignup.description: Who may create a console account.

name.description: The new org name; trimmed, 1 to 100 characters.

currentPassword.description: The user's current password. A user without one leaves it out, and must have signed in within 10 minutes.

newPassword.description: The new password: 8 to 256 characters after Unicode NFKC normalization.

name.description: A new name; trimmed, 1 to 100 characters.

identifier.description: A new host pattern or app ID; see `Platform.identifier`.

UpdatePlatformRequest.description: Changes to a platform. Its type never changes.

name.description: The new project name; trimmed, 1 to 100 characters.

email.description: The new email, trimmed, at most 320 characters. Unique in the project, ignoring case.

emailVerified.description: True marks the new email verified; it is unverified otherwise. Defaults to false.

UpdateUserEmailRequest.description: Changes a user's email at once, without a confirmation email.

email.description: The email, as typed at sign up; null for a user without one.

emailVerified.description: Whether the email has been verified. Also the access token's `email_verified` claim.

emailVerifiedAt.description: When the email was verified; null while it is not.

name.description: The display name; null when none was given.

status.description: Whether the user may sign in.

metadata.description: Your own data about the user: a JSON object of at most 16 KB.

lastSignInAt.description: When the user last signed in; null if never.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

UserPage.description: One page of a project's users, newest first.

UserStatus.description: Whether a user may sign in.

VerificationEmailStatus.description: What happened to the verification email of a sign up. The user and session are created whatever it says.

token.description: The `orvano_token` parameter of the emailed link.

VerifyEmailRequest.description: An email verification, with the token from the emailed link.

consoleSession.name: orvano_console
consoleSession.description:
A console account's session: the `orvano_console` cookie (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`), set by
`consoleAccount.create` and `consoleAccount.createSession`. Browsers send it themselves.

bearer.description: A signed in user's access token: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`, an ES256 JWT.

apiKey.name: X-Orvano-Key
apiKey.description: A server's API key: `X-Orvano-Key: orv_sk_...`, holding the scopes the operation needs.
